newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lower 1996 aluminium output seen at Germany's VAW.
newsitem.headline: Lower 1996 aluminium output seen at Germany's VAW.

text.p: VAW aluminium AG expects to produce 317,000 tonnes of primary aluminum at its German operations this year, compared with 377,000 in 1995, board member Karl Wobbe said in a telephone interview on Tuesday.

Including production at VAW overseas shareholdings in Aluminerie Alouette Inc in Canada (42,000 tonnes) and Tomago Aluminium Ltd in Australia (48,000), the 1996 figure should be 407,000 tonnes versus 416,000 in 1995, he added.
VAW is a unit of utility group Viag AG.
VAW reduced its nominal capacity in Germany by 90,000 tonnes per year to 320,000 tonnes in Germany under the 1994 producer memorandum of understanding (MOU).
It gradually phased out its smelter in Toeging and finally shut it down on February 1, 1996.
The smelter ran at 30,000 tonnes in 1995.
Wobbe said orders were looking up and this strength would continue into 1997, but returns from sales were not satisfactory.
The company depended on dollar-denominated earnings, but had high mark costs to comply with environmental standards and to buy energy locally.
VAW's German capacity was broken down into 210,000 tonnes per year at Rheinwerk, 70,000 at Elbewerk and a 33 percent share in Hamburger Aluminium Werk translated into 40,000 tonnes.
